project_metadata.job_description:
I have a manuscript which I would like to publish as a paperback. Its around 8K words. This book is related to new parents. I can give more insight once we connect further.

I am new to publishing world. As you are working as an editor, could you help me in clarifying the steps needed for me to successfully publish this as a paperback ? 

Let me know if you would be interested in this task.

Thanks,
Puja

Hello [FREELANCER_NAME_001], thanks for getting back to me.

I am a mother, and this book draws both from my own experiences and experiences borrowed from others. It explains how new parents can establish boundaries without having awkward conversations, as well as how visitors should behave around a newborn and the new parents. It is a guide addressing the question every exhausted new Indian parent struggles to answer: 'When can you visit, how long can you stay, and please don't kiss my baby.' I have included checklists, Do's & Don'ts tables, and several anecdotes. This is my first experience as an author, so I would value your support in successfully publishing the paperback. Essentially, I need help fine-tuning the book so that readers find it delightful and then getting it published successfully.

Could you please assist me with the following:
1\. What approach should we take?
2\. What would the price and timelines be?

2\. Regarding this section, " The thing I needed most from my partner was not grand gestures. Sometimes, I needed him to answer the door when people came. messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Thank you for going through the manuscript and accepting the edits. I saw the highlighted portions as well, so there’s no need to worry; I’ll check them carefully as I prepare the final version.

In response to your questions:

1\. The wording "So, I used to eat before anyone or sometimes after everytime, basically it was on demand." does not sound grammatically natural. I recommend:

"So, I ate whenever I was hungry. Sometimes I ate before everyone else, and sometimes afterwards. My meals were completely on demand."

It preserves what you mean while allowing the passage to flow much more smoothly.

2\. You are completely right. As currently phrased, it sounds like you wanted those things to happen rather than recounting what you actually experienced. Because this is your personal story, I recommend wording it like this:

"The thing I needed most from my partner was not grand gestures. He answered the door when visitors arrived. He made sure my water bottle was always filled and within my reach. Sometimes he would simply check in on me, give me a hug, or put a blanket over me. He managed the visitors so I didn't have to. They were small acts, but they meant everything."

This version makes it clear that your partner really did these things for you.

The writing comes across as warm, relatable, and accessible, and I think many new parents will recognize themselves in what you experienced. My only recommendation would be to tighten a few repetitive passages in a future edition. Taken as a whole, it is a lovely book that offers genuine help.

2\. Regarding images: My preference would be to use them sparingly. A handful of simple illustrations or icons at the start of the chapters could look very nice, but I would avoid including too many. Your writing should remain the main focus, and a clean, elegant layout would give the book a more professional feel.
